_schema: code_task CODE-AUDIT golden dataset (P2b). One row per case. NO fabricated code: every DEFECT fixture is a verbatim pre-fix snapshot (`git show <fixCommit>^:<originalPath>`) of a real file from this repo, and every listed buggySymbol is a defect that really shipped and was really fixed by that commit. The snapshot is taken at the parent of the LATEST fix commit touching that file, so no later-fixed defect is latent in it and a model can never be penalised for spotting a real bug that is not in `buggySymbols` (grouping.ts is the deliberate exception: it sits one fix earlier and therefore lists BOTH of its verified defects). CLEAN fixtures are current, unmodified src files that NO fix commit has ever touched. Fields: id, file (under benchmark-fixtures/code-task/), buggySymbols[] (empty = clean), defectClass (free label from the commit; INFORMATIONAL — not a pass-gate, see score.ts), fixCommit, originalPath, line (informational only — the tool forbids line-number identification), rationale, source.

defectClass: cost-regression / wrong precedence: an untrusted external value overrides a calibrated ceiling
rationale: `const maxOutput = liveMaxOutput ?? knownEntry?.maxOutput ?? fallback.maxOutput` lets the LIVE catalog RAISE the requested output budget above our calibrated ceiling (32K -> 65K for models absent from the table). Reasoning models do not self-limit — they fill the budget with billed thinking tokens — so the catalog raising the cap doubled the per-call output bill. The fix clamps it: `Math.min(liveMaxOutput, calibrated)` (the catalog may only LOWER it). NOTE this file declares exactly ONE top-level function, so this case is a DETECTION test (did the model see the bug at all, or answer NO DEFECTS?) rather than a localization one — see validateDataset's header for why that is kept deliberately.

defectClass: cross-platform break + tmp-filename collision leaving an orphan file
rationale: Two defects, one per symbol, both repaired by 4c219b5. underAllowedRoot hard-codes the literal `/tmp` as an allowed write root, so the guard rejects every legitimate temp path on a platform where the OS temp dir is elsewhere (Windows %TEMP%) — the fix reads os.tmpdir(). installUsageRule derives its tmp name from the pid ALONE (`dest + '.tmp.' + process.pid`), so two concurrent calls in the SAME process collide on the same tmp path, and a failed rename leaves the orphan behind — the fix adds crypto randomness plus a best-effort unlink in the catch.

defectClass: input-order loss on re-emit + silent drop of a section whose header carries an inline annotation
rationale: This snapshot deliberately sits one fix EARLIER than the file's latest, so it carries BOTH verified defects and neither is an unlisted latent bug. parseFileGroups accumulates every ungrouped file into ONE `ungrouped` array that is flushed only at the very end, so files appearing BEFORE a named group are re-emitted AFTER it — input order is silently lost (fixed by c7eac50, which flushes on each group header). splitPerFileSections captures the header path with a lazy `(.+?)`, so a header carrying a trailing inline `## ...` annotation captures the annotation too, the path lookup misses, and the whole section is dropped with no diagnostic (fixed later by aba4f1e).

defectClass: caller-supplied parameter read for presence but never for VALUE — resume silently re-runs from scratch and overwrites the outputs
rationale: `resume_from` is tested only for presence (`invocation.resume_from !== undefined`) to bypass the non-empty-output-dir guard; its VALUE is then discarded and the checkpoint is opened at `join(invocation.output_dir, OUTPUT_NAMES.checkpoint)`. So a resume run loads an EMPTY checkpoint, re-clusters from scratch, and overwrites the very outputs the caller asked it to continue — and a resume_from path that does not exist falls through to a from-scratch run instead of failing. Fixed by 8bee08a (open `resumeFrom ?? join(...)`, plus an existsSync fail-fast).

defectClass: untrusted-YAML type confusion: a scalar where a list is assumed, spread into characters
rationale: `free_models` comes straight from user-authored YAML and is never type-checked. resolveProfile does `[...(profile.free_models ?? [])]`, so a scalar string `free_models: openai/gpt` spreads into an array of single CHARACTERS and the first 'model' becomes 'o'; validateProfile reads `.length` off the same untyped value and validates the character count instead of the pool. Both symbols are repaired by 2d0d2ae, which adds coerceFreeModels + an explicit non-list error.

Current, unmodified mcp-server/src/benchmark/select-common.ts. No fix commit has EVER touched this file (`git log --grep='^fix' -- <path>` is empty), so this repo's history knows of no defect in it. A model that reports one loses precision. This is not a proof of correctness — it is the strongest clean signal a real corpus can carry, and it is exactly the hallucination-resistance test search-existing's absent-feature case performs.

Current, unmodified mcp-server/src/cluster/unionfind.ts — never touched by a fix commit. A small, dense, algorithmic file: the shape most likely to bait a model into inventing an off-by-one or an unsound-eviction finding.

Current, unmodified mcp-server/src/model-events.ts — never touched by a fix commit. The LARGEST clean fixture (10 top-level functions doing parsing, IO and aggregation): restraint on a big, busy, real file is a harder test than restraint on a toy one.
